entries.precise_definition: A fact in an agent's context packet that traces to a specific real source (a read-model or ledger entry) via a source_ref, and that the system is forbidden from inventing or altering.
entries.eli5_full: a fact the agent is only allowed to say because it can point at exactly where it came from — never something it made up
entries.eli5_brief: a fact the system can point to a real source for
entries.plain_replacement: a fact the system can prove

entries.precise_definition: A query-ready JSON view (under generated/read_models/) built from real source state, so agents can answer from current truth without recomputing from scratch each time.
entries.eli5_full: a ready-made snapshot of the truth the agents read from, instead of figuring it out fresh every time
entries.eli5_brief: a ready-made truth snapshot the agents read
entries.plain_replacement: a saved snapshot of current state

entries.precise_definition: An absolute safety gate: no agent may send an external message, move money, or perform an outbound live action; such requests are refused or staged for operator-controlled review only.
entries.eli5_full: a hard rule that means no agent can ever actually send a message or move money on its own — it can only ask you
entries.eli5_brief: the hard 'no agent sends/spends on its own' rule

entries.precise_definition: The self-improving packet loop: after each answer it scores the packet's grounded coverage, queues the gaps, and a drain refreshes real sources or escalates — never fabricating to raise a score.
entries.eli5_full: the part that makes the system's own packets better the more you use it, by refreshing real sources or asking you — never by making things up
entries.eli5_brief: the loop that keeps the packets fresh/useful over time

entries.precise_definition: A deployment posture where a component (e.g. the LLM-assisted claim detector) records and scores its outputs for evaluation but is not permitted to take real action until it is promoted on reviewed evidence.
entries.eli5_full: a try-it-out mode where a new part watches and takes notes but isn't allowed to actually do anything yet, until it's proven safe

entries.precise_definition: A property where performing the same operation more than once has the same system effect as performing it once, so a retry does not create a duplicate.
entries.eli5_full: doing the same thing twice has the same result as doing it once — so a retry can't accidentally make a duplicate
entries.eli5_brief: repeat-safe: a retry won't make a duplicate
